newsitem.title: UK: Ashdown calls for independent UK food commission.
newsitem.headline: Ashdown calls for independent UK food commission.

text.p: British Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown called on Monday for the establishment of an independent food commission.
It would take over responsibility for food safety, following the rash of scares which have hit the UK food industry.

"What we need is a stand alone, independent commission which, like the Audit Commission, reports to parliament not ministers and is strong enough to fight its corner in a market place against increasingly powerful players," he said in a speech at the Oxford Farming Conference dinner.

But national bodies alone would be insufficient, he said. "We will need a co-ordinating EU structure powerful enough to stand up to the supra national, as an essential compliment to effective national bodies," he said.

The chief lesson of the past year, during which the UK food and farming industry had reeled from the mad cow (BSE) crisis, was that farmers and consumers had to find the means to empower themselves in their own market once again, he said.
"Farmers teaming up with consumers offers the only chance you both have to win back control of your markets from the multi-nationals, the mega-marketers and the politicians, Ashdown said.
"Farmers need to recognise that in the drive to re-connect farming with its markets and its environment, consumers should be their ally, not their enemy," he said.
The crisis over the mad cow disease BSE had created fear among consumers. "Of course the consumer is prone to panic. What do you expect?, Ashdown asked.

"Ignorance about food, combined with statements of certainty from politicians and scientists which prove false within months of their making have created such a climate of fear that many consumers are readier to believe a passing scare in a tabloid newspaper than any number of weighty scientific reports or ministerial statements given with the full dignity of a House of Commons despatch box," he said.
